words.prose: {{ar:إِنِّى}} ({{tr:innī}}) opens the ayah as emphatic first-person testimony, not as a neutral continuation: the same record-recipient from 69:19 now explains his confidence in his own voice. The fused particle and pronoun make assertion and speaker identity arrive together before the cognition verb. A boundary reading also lets the prior record-word's pause-ending (69:19) flow into this opening, so the displayed record and the explanation of certainty can be heard as one continuous speech act. The later inner inna-class particle creates a nested assertion: the speaker affirms at the speech level and then frames the believed content inside that affirmation.

topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as an inna-class particle with a first-person suffix, and the cross-reference evidence keeps the speaker tied to the quoted record-recipient from 69:19.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the testimony has two assertion layers: the speaker asserts his stance, and the inner clause asserts the content he had held to be true.
topics.reason: The local syntax has an outer inna-clause and an embedded inna-class complement, so the row's nesting claim is structurally licensed.

words.gloss_range: a past first-person cognition verb locally narrowed toward settled conviction about the reckoning, while retaining the root's supposition-to-certainty tension

words.prose: {{ar:ظَنَنْتُ}} ({{tr:ẓanantu}}) makes the speaker's earlier inner stance the hinge of the testimony. Its perfect first-person form looks back to a completed conviction whose fulfillment is now being experienced, and its clausal complement means the belief had a full content: that the speaker would meet his own account. The embedded -tu keeps the same I present between the opening assertion, the inner proposition, and the possessed reckoning. The root can move between supposition and certainty, but the meeting-of-reckoning frame narrows the local force toward settled expectation rather than surprise or doubt. Because the verb is Form I, that epistemic range remains the speaker's own stance rather than shifting into a causative sense of making someone doubtful. The same construction echoes certainty-of-meeting language in 2:46 and 2:249, now directed not simply toward encounter but toward the speaker's own reckoning. The repeated nūn sounds around the word add an audible inward pressure to the cognition sequence.

topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect first-person verb, and attachment evidence ties its subject to the same quoted speaker.

words.prose: {{ar:أَنِّي}} ({{tr:annī}}) pivots from the act of believing into the believed scene. It packages the following meeting-account clause as a governed proposition, so the verb of cognition has a definite payload rather than an open-ended thought. Its first-person suffix repeats the speaker inside the embedded content before the encounter role is named, making the expected meeting personal from the start. Because it is an inna-class particle, the embedded proposition is not only subordinated but also strengthened from within, echoing the outer assertion at the start of the ayah.

words.gloss_range: active-participle encounter role: the speaker is characterized as one who will meet or face his account
words.root_gloss_range: range of meeting, encountering, coming face to face, casting or placing before, and related convergence; local Form III participle selects meeting/facing while allowing presentation pressure only as a narrowed image
words.prose: {{ar:مُلَٰقٍ}} ({{tr:mulāqin}}) gives the embedded clause its predicate: the speaker is characterized as one who will meet the account. The participial form makes the encounter a role or state assigned to the speaker, not merely a timed event or a completed finite meeting verb, and its placement before the object lets the clause first establish encounter-status and then land on the personal reckoning. Its light indefinite/defective surface, with final yā suppressed under tanwīn, still carries predicate force and is not merely a genitive dependent. The root's face-to-face meeting branch makes the reckoning feel encountered and arrived at, not merely known as an abstraction. Casting or depositing language in the wider root family is kept narrower here: it can make the account feel presented before the speaker, but the local Form III participle selects meeting/facing. The construction echoes certainty-of-meeting formulas in 2:46 and 2:249, while 69:20 shifts the object from Lord-meeting to account-meeting.

topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as the predicate of the embedded inna-class clause, and QAC identifies it as an active participle.

topics.reason: V4 separates casting from meeting branches, so the casting/depositing material survives only as image pressure around presentation, not as the selected local action.

topics.reason: The distributional profile supports the active participle as a smaller local subset, and the QAC tag confirms the participial form.

words.gloss_range: the speaker's own reckoning/account, functioning as the object met and closing the ayah with a pausal personal ending
words.root_gloss_range: range of counting, accounting, reckoning, calculation, sufficiency/evaluation, and accountability; local context selects personal reckoning while retaining measured audit and evaluative pressure
words.prose: {{ar:حِسَابِيَهْ}} ({{tr:ḥisābiyah}}) is where the whole testimony lands: the expected encounter resolves as the speaker's own account. The possessive suffix makes the reckoning individually definite, while the active participle before it makes that account the thing faced, not just a ledger named in isolation. That final possessive also closes the same first-person chain that began with assertion and passed through conviction. The verbal-noun form can name the reckoning process as well as the resulting account, so the root's counting and reckoning branch keeps the scene concrete as measured audit, and the sufficiency/evaluation branch adds the question of whether the counted result answers the measure without replacing the selected reckoning sense. The cadence moves from the lighter participial -in into the fuller -iyah pause ending, and the final hāʾ al-sakta seals the ayah on a personal pausal ending that matches the prior record-word's ending (69:19), pairing record and reckoning by sound as well as sense. The same word returns in 69:26 with the opposite emotional register, so 69:20 hears the account as confident expectation while 69:26 hears it as dread.

topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the noun the direct object of the active participle and resolves its possessive suffix to the same speaker.

topics.reason: V4 supports counting/reckoning and sufficiency/evaluation branches, but local context selects reckoning/account while preserving sufficiency as evaluative pressure.

topics.reason: QAC marks the form as a verbal noun, and the accepted reckoning senses support both accounting process and account/result.

topics.reason: The surface includes the possessive ending plus hāʾ al-sakta, and the row's pausal claim fits the ayah-ending position.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence ظننت ... ملاق حسابيه joins cognition, encounter, and a first-person account.
baseline_models.mechanism: A conviction formed after an indication points forward to a face-to-face encounter with a personally possessed reckoning.

activation_trace.role: Certainty arising after an indication makes ظننت an evidence-grounded stance rather than a bare guess.
Two things coming face to face turns the future reckoning into a personal encounter.
Counting and reckoning supplies the object that the speaker expects to face.

changed_reading.before: I merely expected that an accounting would happen.
changed_reading.after: I held evidence-grounded certainty that I would personally face the reckoning belonging to me.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ظننت and حسابيه carry overlapping images of inward supposition and reckoning.
baseline_models.mechanism: The mental estimate and the eventual account mirror one another: anticipatory self-reckoning rehearses the external reckoning before it arrives.

activation_trace.role: Uncertain supposition preserves the live risk under which the speaker mentally prepares.
Reckoning as supposition folds the speaker's inward estimate into the noun for the coming account.
Face-to-face meeting supplies the point at which inward estimation confronts its external counterpart.

changed_reading.before: The speaker reports a correct belief about a later audit.
changed_reading.after: The speaker has already begun to account inwardly because he expects his inward estimate to meet an objective account.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The compact construction ملاق حسابيه makes the account something encountered, not merely computed.
baseline_models.mechanism: What has been counted as the speaker's standing arrives as experienced good or ill; account is both assessment and encountered outcome.

activation_trace.role: What one meets of good or ill makes the account arrive as lived consequence.
Counted merits and standing supply the accumulated profile whose consequence is met.
Literal counting keeps the outcome tied to an assessed total rather than free-floating fortune.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Expectation confirmed as certainty.** **ظ ن ن B001** (certainty after an indication) is selected by the successful encounter with **ح س ب B001** (counting and reckoning), and later sharpened by **ي ق ن B001** in 69:51. The packet supplies anticipation, encounter, and settled certainty; I infer that prior signs made the coming audit strongly knowable. `ظننت` reads as reasoned certainty rather than weak guessing.
2. **Risk-bearing supposition preserved.** **ظ ن ن B003** (suspicion or uncertain supposition) remains possible because the statement is retrospective and contrasts with the other person's `لم أدر` in 69:26. The packet supplies unequal epistemic postures; I infer that even incomplete expectation can govern conduct when the account is taken seriously. This weaker reading does not cancel B001; it highlights practical responsiveness under uncertainty.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 69:51's **ي ق ن B001** retrospectively strengthens the certainty branch of `ظننت`, while 69:26 preserves the contrast with failed awareness.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Expectation can be settled conviction.** `ظ ن ن` B001 is "certainty after an indication." The event has become fixed in 69:15, presentation discloses all in 69:18, and the right-hand record yields the favorable sequence in 69:19-24. B001 assigns the speaker's prior `ظَنَنتُ` the role of action-guiding certainty now vindicated. The packet supplies expectation and realized match; I infer that correspondence retrospectively confirms conviction. The line reads as "I lived on the basis that this meeting was real," not as a lucky guess.
2. **Uncertain anticipation remains a distinct viable reading.** `ظ ن ن` B003 is "suspicion or uncertain supposition." Nothing in the form itself erases epistemic risk, and 69:25 immediately supplies the opposite recipient, showing that the outcome was not publicly possessed in advance by everyone. B003 assigns the speaker a posture of preparedness under incomplete access. The packet supplies eventual confirmation; I infer that acting under a serious prospect can prepare one even without full certainty. This reading changes the line into a claim that accountable anticipation, not exhaustive prior knowledge, shaped the speaker.
3. **The account is a face-to-face encounter with managed consequence.** `ل ق ي` B004 is "two things coming face to face" and B007 is "what one meets of good or ill"; `ح س ب` B001 is counting and reckoning, while B006 is "supervision and accountable management." The participle `مُلَاقٍ` makes account an encountered counterpart, and the surrounding book/reward sequence makes reckoning administer lived consequence. The packet supplies record, meeting, and outcome; I infer record -> managed account -> encountered condition. `حِسَابِيَهْ` therefore reads as an administered relation that confronts the person, not only a numerical total.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 69:26's `وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ` creates the decisive contrast unavailable in the local window: serious expectation, whether B001 certainty or B003 uncertainty, differs functionally from non-orientation and confessed ignorance. The late `ي ق ن` B001 in 69:51 confirms the certainty branch without erasing the risk-bearing branch; both prepared the successful speaker for encounter.

facets.statement: Coğrafi kullanım dağ kenarlarındaki çıkıntıları veya iki dağ arasındaki birleşim yerini adlandırır.

Coğrafi aktarım koşullu olarak sorgulanır ve benzer bir biçimin ilk ünsüzü kökün parçası sayılarak bu kökten ayrılır.
